People continue their journey in rainy weather.
Pexels · 12327578
Plans for a rainy day
There is more than one way to change our plans. In my experience, practical preparation and attention to others are
two useful starting points.
One reason is that a backup plan makes a change less disappointing. For instance, we choose a museum when rain
makes the outdoor walk uncomfortable. This prevents a small difficulty from taking over the experience. It also leaves
us more time to notice what is happening.
Another reason is that telling other people early helps everyone adjust. For example, we send a clear message
about the new meeting place before anyone leaves home. This approach recognises that the experience belongs to
more than one person and that different people may need different things.
These examples show why preparation and consideration work well together. We do not have to control every detail.
We can make a sensible arrangement and remain ready to respond.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a focused main idea. Develop one supporting reason in each body paragraph, with a concrete
example. Conclude by connecting the two reasons without introducing a new argument. Use the structure as a model; write
about an experience of your own.
Make a sentence of your own, then answer: What two reasons support the main idea? Explain one example. (Model: The two
reasons are that a backup plan makes a change less disappointing and that telling other people early helps everyone adjust.
One example is that we choose a museum when rain makes the outdoor walk uncomfortable.)
